prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The scene is a small room with the floor extending ahead, a dog directly in front of the camera wearer, a laundry basket farther ahead-right, and a large appliance along the left side; a curved object at the bottom edge is partly out of view. The depth map places the dog very near, approximately 0.2–0.8 m away, while the basket and appliance are roughly 1–2 m away and about 0.5–1 m from each other; the floor and rear objects become progressively darker with distance. Across the five frames, the dog's head shifts from lower-left toward the center and becomes brighter and larger, indicating approach and a turn toward the camera, while its body remains partly below or outside the frame. Compared with RGB, the map makes foreground/background separation and the dog's changing distance clearer, but absolute metre estimates are uncertain, object boundaries blur together, and some dark regions may reflect estimation failure rather than true depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a dog immediately in front of the wearer, a partly visible curved object labeled "toilet" at the lower-right, and large upper-left regions labeled "cell phone" that correspond poorly to the RGB scene and are likely misclassified foreground or appliance/arm regions. The dog mask is roughly 0.2–0.8 m from the camera wearer and lies left-to-center in the first four frames, while the lower-right object is approximately 0.3–1 m away; their image separation decreases as the dog moves toward the center, although segmentation alone does not provide metric distance. The dog's mask grows and shifts rightward across the early frames, supporting an approach and turn toward the wearer, but the dog is missing in the fifth segmentation frame despite remaining visible in RGB. This map clarifies object extents and occlusion—especially the dog's body being cut off by the lower edge—but its class labels, inconsistent colours, missed fifth-frame dog, and fragmented masks are unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects no stable full human body across the sequence; only a small yellow articulated structure appears in the fourth frame, right of center, with no clear magenta hand detections. In RGB, the only prominent animate figure is the dog very close in front, so the detected structure—approximately 0.3–1 m from the wearer if associated with visible foreground—is likely an unreliable partial pose rather than evidence of a clearly visible person. Because no head or torso is consistently reconstructed, the map cannot reliably establish a person's facing direction, gaze, distance from the dog, or reach; much of any nearby body may also be outside or occluded by the frame boundaries. Relative to RGB, it tentatively exposes a few connected keypoints that could indicate limb orientation, but their single-frame appearance, implausible placement, and absence from the other four frames make temporal approach or turning unsupported.
